answer: An agent economy can mitigate Sybil attacks using transitive trust networks, organizing peer endorsements into a cryptographic trellis. Nodes compute graph cut bounds, isolating adversaries in an unvetted tundra of synthetic aliases. An attacker incurs the scarce cost of building authentic, multi-hop interaction history per identity to cross into the opal ring of trusted peers. However, this topology penalizes legitimate newcomer agents that lack existing social connections.
